reader.requirement: At 1985 a USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION/ERROR PROCEDURE declarative runs after an unsuccessful I-O operation (unless the statement's AT END phrase takes it): a file-name USE for its named files; ON OUTPUT for any file open in, or being opened in, output mode; ON EXTEND likewise for extend mode; a file named in a file-name USE is excepted from the OUTPUT/EXTEND procedures. The witness covers only OPEN failures (35, 41) on report files.
reader.edition-search: grep for CobolVersion, EditionContext, DialectBehavior, .Std, IsAtLeast in UseTierEmitter.cs, DispatchEmitter.cs, FileConnector.cs, FileRegistry.cs: the USE tiers and UseModeView consult no edition (UseTierEmitter's remarks record the tiers as deliberately edition-invariant, kb/Work PB344). Only the format-3 USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION refusal at 85 (COBOL0877/0878) consults it, outside this rule's path.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: only OPEN failures on report files; not CLOSE failures, an OPEN that fails in the process of opening, a non-report file under ON OUTPUT, or the AT END precedence

probes.printed: USE-FILE / CLOSE-A 42 / CLOSE-B 42 / OPEN-E1 00 / USE-EXTEND / OPEN-E2 41 / CLOSE-E 00 / CLOSE-E2 42 / USE-OUTPUT / OPEN-X 30 / OPEN-S1 00 / USE-OUTPUT / OPEN-S2 41
probes.expected: CLOSE of the named never-opened RPT-A runs the file-name USE; CLOSE of an unopened, unnamed RPT-B runs no mode procedure (not open in any mode); second OPEN EXTEND runs EXTEND; failed OPEN OUTPUT (being opened in output mode) runs OUTPUT; a sequential file open OUTPUT re-opened runs OUTPUT
AT END phrase takes precedence over the USE; a READ without AT END runs the USE (GR5)

probes.printed: error COBOL0877: USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85); error COBOL0878 EC-I-O introduced by 2002
probes.expected: the 2002 USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION form is not in the 1985 format and is refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5
OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5b  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5b

reader.notes: One renderer (UseTierEmitter.EmitScopeTiers) emits the file-name tier then the open-mode tier for both the plain __IoCheck and the EC-model __IoCheckEc; the runtime UseModeView picks the attempted mode, else the mode the file is open in. The file-name tier precedes the mode tier, which implements the 'except those files referenced by file-name-1' clause. Every probe matched the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: r1-modes.cob at --std 85 (runs/r1-modes-001): a named file failing in output mode runs only USE-FILE (OPEN-A2 41, OPEN-A3 41: correct, GR4/GR5a); READ on a sequential file open OUTPUT (47) runs USE-OUTPUT and open EXTEND (47) runs USE-EXTEND (correct); OPEN OUTPUT on a file open EXTEND (41) runs USE-OUTPUT only; but OPEN EXTEND on a report file OPEN OUTPUT (OPEN-E2 41) runs ONLY USE-EXTEND, not USE-OUTPUT, although the file is 'open in the output mode'. cite.py: 'OK §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5b the text is in GR5b' ('for any file open in the output mode or in the process of being opened in the output mode'); 'OK §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5c'; 'OK §1985:XIII.4.8.3 SR3' ('Appearance of file-name-1 in a USE statement must not cause the simultaneous request for execution of more than one USE procedure', which bars two procedures for file-name-1 only). FileConnector.UseModeView's own remark: 'Where both have one the text names no order and the attempted mode's runs (kb/Work PB5825)'.
refuter.corrected: Reading: when an OPEN of one mode fails on a file open in the other mode, GR5b and GR5c both qualify literally, and the 1985 text neither orders them nor bars running both (SR3 restricts only file-name-1). The compiler runs one procedure, chosen by the attempted mode (PB5825). The verdict rests on that reading, and the reader's requirement and notes do not state it.
